definition: A defined character, tone, or set of behavioral traits that a language model is instructed or trained to adopt during interactions.
details: Personas are commonly configured via system prompts or fine-tuning, shaping how a model communicates (formal vs. casual, concise vs. detailed) without necessarily changing its underlying knowledge or reasoning ability.

explainer.lead: A persona is the character or tone a language model is told or trained to adopt. It matters because teams use personas to control how a model communicates without retraining the model itself.

tiers.eli5: It's like giving a robot a costume and a script: the robot knows the same things, but it talks like a pirate instead of a professor.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set personas in system prompts or through fine-tuning to fix tone, verbosity, and style. A common pitfall is assuming a persona changes what the model knows or how well it reasons.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a character, tone, or set of behavioral traits a model is instructed or trained to adopt. It shapes communication style, not necessarily underlying knowledge or reasoning ability.

explainer.example: A support bot is given a system prompt to reply in a friendly, concise tone, so the same model answers a billing question in two sentences rather than a long essay.
